evidence.note: Nonce in the ID token belongs to an earlier authorization request, not the current one.
Token was issued at the evaluation time and is otherwise within its window (exp is 1 hour later), so expiry is not the cause.

output.fix: Generate a fresh, single-use nonce (and state) for every authorization request. Store it server-side or in a session-bound cookie, and compare it to the ID token's nonce on callback. A login page left open overnight is likely reusing a cached auth URL or a nonce from an older tab. Regenerate the authorization request when the page is stale or reloaded, or when the user submits. Give the stored nonce a short TTL and send the user back through a new login if it has expired. Keep the nonce check, signature validation and clock skew of 5 minutes or less.

alternatives.why_not: iat/nbf equal the reference time and exp is one hour later, so the token is within its validity window.
